source.title: Weight-based Decomposition: A Case for Bilinear MLPs
source.authors: Michael T. Pearce; Thomas Dooms; Alice Rigg

record.tranche_reason: The paper analyzes eigenvector features in bilinear MLPs, not individual neurons or the neuron-level behavior named in the claim versions. Its eigenvector interpretations are related but do not test those versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports qualitative interpretations of eigenvectors, including examples it calls partly polysemantic. These are features in a bilinear-model decomposition, not measurements of neurons as named by the claim versions, so they are recorded under fits_no_version. The paper's regularization comparisons concern feature appearance, not a measured change in polysemantic-neuron share. Comparisons or results cited from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper introduces a weight-based eigendecomposition for bilinear MLPs and interprets eigenvectors, not neurons. It reports no rate or measurement of polysemantic neurons in vision or language models. Its mentions of polysemanticity concern eigenvectors and are speculative, e.g. sparse inputs will 'likely encourage polysemanticity'. Regularization results concern visual cleanliness of eigenvector features, not neuron polysemanticity share. So it neither tests nor relies on any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that bilinear MLPs can be decomposed, exactly, into sparsely interacting eigenvectors. Top eigenvectors appear largely interpretable for MNIST and preliminarily for Tiny Stories, and small-eigenvalue terms can be truncated with under 1% accuracy loss. Latent noise and weight decay give more interpretable features. TinyLlama-1.1B can be finetuned into a bilinear variant. Eigenvectors are not expected to be fully monosemantic and may need combining with SAEs.
record.recipe_differences: The paper introduces a weight-based eigendecomposition for bilinear MLPs rather than using the original sources' neuron-activation approaches.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper qualitatively reports that regularization changes eigenvector appearance: latent noise removes peripheral values and noisiness, and weight decay further cleans up features. It does not measure polysemantic-neuron rates.

fits_no_version.finding: Bilinear-MLP eigenvectors in MNIST models are largely interpretable, but some mix different digit slants across positive and negative components. The authors attribute this to XOR-like squared activation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight-derived eigenvector features of bilinear layers can be polysemantic through the sign structure of a squared activation.

fits_no_version.finding: Tiny Stories 'swim' eigenvectors are mostly monosemantic in their top activations. One (Pos1) mixes 'love to' and clothing contexts that share a pool or water context.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Bilinear-LM eigenvectors are mostly monosemantic, with occasional mixtures of related contexts.

record.problems: The interpretability findings are qualitative and based on selected examples; no quantitative rate or systematic score of polysemanticity is reported. The Tiny Stories model uses a simplified, single-layer setup and a custom tokenizer and dataset preprocessing.
record.rows_left_out: No otherwise eligible neuron-level results were reported. Cited findings from other work and the paper's regularization results on visual feature appearance were not entered as claim-version rows.

untested.parts: Neuron responses to unrelated inputs in image classifiers. The MNIST models are analysed only via eigenvectors.
Share of polysemantic MLP neurons in transformer LMs, and how it varies by layer.
Superposition as the cause. Only a speculative remark links input sparsity to eigenvector polysemanticity.
Polysemanticity from initialization, regularization or training noise without capacity pressure.
Change in polysemantic-neuron share with activation, architecture or regularization. The bilinear vs SiLU loss comparison has no polysemanticity measure.
Reinterpretation of canonical polysemantic neurons as one shared feature.
Dependence of neuron polysemanticity on activation range or explanation scoring.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's relation and T6 are appropriate. Row states should be cannot_determine rather than observed, since no version applies. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Neuron responses to multiple unrelated image inputs in image classifiers.
The prevalence of polysemantic MLP neurons in transformer language models.
Whether neuron polysemanticity is caused by representing more sparse features than available neurons.
Polysemantic neurons arising from initialization, regularization, or training noise when capacity is sufficient.
Changes in the share of polysemantic neurons across activation functions, architectures, or regularization, and any performance cost of reducing that share.
Whether canonical polysemantic neurons resolve into one shared feature or related jobs when examined with better tools.
Whether neuron polysemanticity depends on activation range or explanation scoring.

rows.subject: MNIST model
rows.stage_stated: trained; training details in Appendix A
rows.operation_detail: Interpreted input-space eigenvectors from the bilinear model weights.
rows.measure: Qualitative interpretation of eigenvector input features.
rows.value: The top eigenvectors appear largely interpretable; many resemble full digits, while others emphasize parts. For digit 1, some positive eigenvectors contain 1-like features at different slants.
rows.note: These are eigenvector features, not individual neurons.
rows.check: Eigenvector features of a bilinear MNIST model, not neurons. The 'observed' state has no referent among the claim versions.

rows.subject: Fashion-MNIST model
rows.stage_stated: trained; training details in Appendix A
rows.operation_detail: Interpreted input-space eigenvectors from the bilinear model weights.
rows.measure: Qualitative interpretation of eigenvector input features.
rows.value: Eigenvectors focus more on specific parts, including neck and sleeve areas for shirts, pullovers, and coats, and the leg gap for trousers.
rows.note: This is a qualitative interpretation of eigenvector features, not a neuron-level polysemanticity measurement.
rows.check: Eigenvector features, not neurons. Qualitative description with no polysemanticity measure relevant to any version.

top activations, excluding the separately described Pos1

rows.measure: Qualitative interpretation of top eigenvector activations.
rows.value: The top activations are described as mostly monosemantic, with examples involving aquatic animals as subjects and non-swimming contexts for water.
rows.note: The paper describes eigenvectors, not individual neurons.
rows.check: Eigenvectors of a Tiny Stories bilinear MLP, described as mostly monosemantic. These are not MLP neurons, so the row does not bear on V2.

rows.subject: single-layer Tiny Stories model
rows.stage_stated: trained on Tiny Stories; training details in Appendix C
rows.operation_detail: Interpreted the Pos1 eigenvector for a selected output direction using weight-based eigendecomposition.

conditions.value: “swim” unembedding minus the average unembedding of listed other verbs

rows.measure: Qualitative interpretation of top eigenvector activations and contexts.
rows.value: Pos1 is described as somewhat polysemantic: it activates for “love to” contexts and clothing-related contexts, both associated with a broader pool-or-water context.
rows.note: The authors identify a shared broader context for these eigenvector activations; this is not a test of neuron-level polysemanticity.
rows.check: A single eigenvector (Pos1) called 'somewhat polysemantic'. It is a selected example, not a neuron, and gives no rate.
